summary:
FieldShift is a decision-support web app that helps farmers adapt to climate change. It combines NASA POWER climate data, live weather forecasts, soil moisture, soil test results, crop characteristics and market data to give simple, location-based advice.

After entering their province, district and field size, farmers get:

A day-by-day irrigation plan for each plot (irrigate, no need, or wait for rain), with water volume and cost, plus optional automatic irrigation
Storm, frost, heat and flood warnings, with disaster checklists
Soil analysis that interprets lab results, recommends suitable crops and calculates fertilizer needs
Crop rotation advice that protects soil health
Seasonal disease and pest alerts, and community reports that detect outbreaks nearby
A market section showing world and Türkiye production, high-demand crops and a profit-oriented crop ranking
An AI assistant that answers questions and analyses plant photos
A library of 94 crops and 236 varieties
Expense and harvest tracking that flags unnecessary spraying and over-irrigation

FieldShift helps farmers save water, protect their soil, cut costs and choose the right crop.
From satellite to field, from data to decision.
details: FieldShift is a decision-support web app for farmers, built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. It turns satellite and weather data into concrete advice a farmer can act on. Should I irrigate today? How much water? What should I plant? Which risk is coming? The app is a single HTML file that opens in Chrome with no installation, and it works in English and Turkish. The problem it solves In Türkiye, agriculture uses most of the country’s water, and much irrigation is still done by calendar or by eye. That wastes water, energy and money. Small farmers rarely have easy access to satellite data, weather models or an agronomist. FieldShift brings this information together on one screen, in plain language. Data sources and methods Weather and soil moisture: 7-day forecasts and modelled soil moisture from Open-Meteo, which uses models such as ECMWF and DWD ICON. Long-term climate: NASA POWER, based on satellite and MERRA-2 data. Offline fallback: regional climate averages for all 81 provinces. Water needs (FAO methods): evapotranspiration (ET₀) by the Hargreaves method crop coefficients (Kc) effective rainfall field capacity and irrigation thresholds by soil type Market data: FAOSTAT, the OECD-FAO Agricultural Outlook 2025–2034, TÜİK 2026 estimates, TMO and Trakya Birlik purchase prices, and 2026–27 support payments. Sections 🏠 Home Weather and a 7-day forecast. Storm and heavy-rain days get a red, blinking warning. Land in active use (%) and average soil moisture. Water in the soil (m³). A day-by-day irrigation plan for the week. “What should I do today?” advice. 🗺️ My Plots: You split the field into plots and give each one a crop, soil type and irrigation method (drip, sprinkler, flood or dryland). Each plot shows: a moisture meter with its irrigation threshold its seasonal water need “Irrigate now” and automatic irrigation switches a “What should I plant here?” suggestion When an action isn’t possible, the app explains why. For example, it says why a dryland plot can’t be irrigated. 📡 Devices: A weather station, soil moisture sensors, solenoid valves and field cameras, with temperature and humidity shown beside each camera. These are demo devices fed by real data. You can also connect a real sensor over USB with an Arduino or ESP32. 🧪 Soil Test: Enter pH, salinity, lime, organic matter, phosphorus, potassium, zinc and iron. The app: interprets the values lists the crops that suit the soil and the ones that don’t gives a fertilizer plan per decare It can also read a photo of the lab report with AI. 👥 My Region: Farmers report the diseases, pests and disasters they see. When nearby reports of the same problem increase, the app warns of an outbreak. It shows the solutions neighbours tried and how often each one worked. A seasonal calendar gives early warnings for 40 diseases and pests. Preparedness guides cover 9 natural disasters: storm, flood, drought, frost, heat wave, fire, landslide, heavy snow and earthquake. 📈 Market & Demand: Shows the most produced crops in the world and in Türkiye, plus the crops with a supply gap. It ranks crops by how much they would benefit the farmer: 35% suitability for the field 25% market demand 15% government support 15% water saving 10% soil health It also estimates income per decare. 🤖 AI Assistant: Diagnoses plant diseases from photos, estimates harvest timing and answers free-form questions. Without a Claude API key, a basic mode still answers using your farm’s data. 🌿 Crop Library: 94 crops and 236 varieties. Each crop has its planting and harvest times, water need, ideal temperature, pH, salt tolerance, nitrogen effect, growing steps and common diseases. 💰 Costs & Harvest: Tracks irrigation and other costs, harvest income and net profit. It also flags unnecessary costs, such as: spraying by calendar spraying on a rainy day using more water than the crop needs Notifications: You get alerts for dry or waterlogged soil, storms, frost and regional outbreaks. The browser needs to stay open, but the tab can be in the background. Technical structure One HTML/JavaScript file. Data is stored in the browser (localStorage). One button switches between English and Turkish, and saved records are converted to the new language. In the claude.ai version, regional reports are really shared between farmers who use the app. Limitations The Devices tab is a demo. Getting notifications while the app is fully closed would require hosting it on a server, as a PWA with a push service. AI advice is advisory only. Farmers should consult their provincial or district agriculture directorate before using pesticides. Impact Switching to drip irrigation and irrigating by the forecast can clearly cut water use, by around 30–50%. Choosing the right crop at the start of the season, avoiding unnecessary spraying and preparing for disasters ahead of time lower both the farmer’s costs and risks. I can turn this into a shareable document for your competition presentation or project report if you’d like.
